history.summary: D18 Simei 3BR (1,206sqft) at $1.45M / $1,202psf — priced exactly at URA median and the cheapest absolute entry in the batch. Strong 7.32%/yr CAGR on 131 txns and big CDL-built space, but 1.74km (21-min walk) from MRT is a serious liquidity/rental handicap.
history.rating_rationale: The price is honest ($1,202psf = URA median exactly) and the $1.45M entry is in an accessible band with a deep HDB-upgrader pool in D18. 7.32%/yr CAGR on 131 transactions is reliable and well above the OCR ~3.7% baseline. CDL build, well-maintained, spacious 1,206sqft. The hard problem is transit: 1.74km / 21-min walk to Upper Changi DTL (shuttle bus only) materially caps both rental yield and resale appeal versus MRT-fronting peers. Built 2005, so ~20yr old with ~79yrs lease left. Decent value play, but the MRT distance keeps it from a Buy — Neutral.

history.summary: Well-built, well-managed CDL development (648 units) at a low $1124 PSF, below median, with a strong 7.36% CAGR over 131 transactions. The fatal flaw for an investment hold is connectivity: 1.74km from Upper Changi MRT (shuttle-bus dependent), which caps tenant demand and resale to a car-owning niche. A solid home, a middling investment.
history.rating_rationale: Genuine strengths — CDL build quality, proactive management, deep 648-unit liquidity, below-median PSF ($1124 vs $1206), and 7.36% CAGR over a healthy 131 transactions. But location is the binding constraint: at 1.74km/21min to the nearest MRT it relies on a shuttle bus, which structurally limits the tenant pool (transit-dependent renters skip it) and resale appeal. At 21 years old (~78yr lease remaining) lease decay is starting to matter. The appreciation rate likely reflects a low base off the 2005 vintage rather than a durable forward catalyst.

history.summary: A confirmed 3BR (the bed-count challenge is a false alarm — 1,238sf is this project's modal 3BR) in a large, deeply liquid, well-proven Simei leasehold with one of the strongest exit records available: 94.7% of 719 resales sold at a profit. The problem is not the asset, it is the ask. Read against the RIGHT cohort — the 1,238sf layout's own prints of $1,467k (Feb-26), $1,468,888 (Mar-26) and $1,473k (Jun-26) — $1.50M is +1.8% above the most this layout has EVER fetched, and this exact unit has already sat unsold for 66 days (listed 7 Jun at $1,535k, cut once) against six other standing 3BR asks in the same project. Sound asset, no edge at the ask.
history.rating_rationale: FORMAT SETTLED FIRST — the 3BR label is CORRECT and the psf is NOT a size-mix artifact. URA rental filings put 123 of this project's 154 3BR contracts in the 1,200-1,300sf band, with ZERO 2BR contracts ever filed there (the 2BR core is 900-1,100sf, 27 of 33 contracts). The bed_bands 'contested' flag is a containment false positive: the 2BR band's 1,350 upper edge is dragged up by a 6-contract 1,300-1,400 tail that has no matching sale stock at all (exactly one sale print exists in 1,300-1,399, versus 53 prints at 1,200-1,299 and 16 at 900-1,099). So the cohort is right — but reading the discount against the right cohort removes it. Within the 3BR grid there are three distinct price tiers by near-identical size: 1,206sf ~$1,155psf, 1,238sf ~$1,187psf, 1,227sf ~$1,206-1,256psf. The subject is the 1,238 tier, whose last three prints sit within $6k of each other ($1,467k / $1,468,888 / $1,473k). At $1,211psf the ask is above all of them. The -3.7% 'discount' vs age-adjusted D18 peers is inside noise and largely the level of a 21-year-old leasehold in a non-prime pocket, not a dislocation. DECISIVE FIND: this is not a fresh listing. 31 Simei Rise / 1,238sf appeared 7 Jun 2026 at $1,535,000 under listing 500079722 (agent Ryan Heng) and is now $1,500,000 — 66 days unsold, one 2.3% cut, still above the layout's record print, while six other 3BR asks stand in the same project ($1.45M-$1.65M) and a 1,206sf at $1.45M has likewise sat since 7 Jun. Absorption at these ask levels is slow; the project clears, but below them. WHAT CARRIES THE SCORE IS THE DE-WEIGHTED INPUT: score_1000 662's largest component is appreciation +9.97 off a 7.32% trailing CAGR. I verified that CAGR is real and not the pooled size-mix artifact (same-size 1,227sf went $839psf Aug-21 to $1,256psf Jul-26, ~8.4%/yr) — but the repo's own backtest says trailing CAGR carries ~no forward power, momentum is -0.581, and this layout's own 2026 prints are flat ($1,467k Feb to $1,473k Jun, +0.4% in four months). Re-scored at a realistic 4.0%/yr the listing lands 611, and 5yr annualized ROI falls from 7.18% to 4.26%. GENUINE POSITIVES, kept honest: the exit record is deep-book evidence, not a thin-book 5.0 — 719 resales, only 40 losses in 24 years, avg holding 7.0yrs, 341 of 719 above 6% annualized; liquidity is excellent (648 units, 53 prints in the subject's size band alone, 50+ deals last year, 47% HDB buyers from the Tampines/Simei MOP pool); and OCR is the region the backtest favours. I also CORRECTED an error I inherited from my own June evaluations: PropertyGuru's '1.74km / 21 min, shuttle-bus dependent' is wrong — realsmart puts Upper Changi DT34 at 738m and Tampines East DT33 at 851m, 99.co says 0.9km/12min, and the scorer's own geocode returns 832m. Two Downtown Line stations inside a ~12-minute walk. That makes MMR's -8.34 MRT penalty too harsh (correcting it alone lifts the score to 688) and retires the 'fatal connectivity flaw' framing of the June calls. NET: a sound, liquid, well-proven asset with no value edge at $1.50M. The distance between Neutral and Buy here is about $35-45k of price, not the quality of the building. At $1,455,000-1,470,000 — which a 66-day sit and a seller already cutting suggests is reachable — this is a fair-to-good OCR entry. At the ask you are paying more than anyone has ever paid for this layout, funded by 2.13% net carry, on a lease that will be ~67yrs and a building ~28yrs old at exit.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Well-evidenced and unexciting. URA rental filings give $4,450/mo off 31 contracts (confidence 0.95), and realsmart independently confirms three June-2026 3BR contracts in the 1,200-1,300sf band at $4,300-$4,400, project est. yield 3.4%. That puts gross at 3.56% and net at 2.13% — thin carry that will not fund a 5-7yr hold, though per the repo's priors a low gross yield is mildly favourable for forward price growth rather than a negative. Tenant demand is genuine but ordinary: a ~12-min walk to two Downtown Line stations serves Changi Business Park, SUTD and the airport corridor well, and the CBD poorly (~35-40min on the DTL). Rent is a floor here, not a thesis.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: The trailing 7.32%/yr is real, not a size-mix artifact — I checked the same-size series specifically because pooled CAGRs mislead in projects with a wide unit mix, and 1,227sf ran $839psf (Aug-21) to $1,256psf (Jul-26), ~8.4%/yr. But that is one bull regime, the repo's own backtest gives trailing CAGR ~no forward power, momentum is -0.581, and the subject's own layout has gone flat in 2026 ($1,467k Feb -> $1,473k Jun, +0.4% in four months) even as the project median psf rose 4.4% year-on-year. Forward I would underwrite ~4.0%/yr: the D18/OCR baseline plus a modest liquidity and MOP-demand edge, minus lease decay on a 73-year tail. That is the number the override reflects, and it takes 5yr annualized ROI from an implausible 7.18% to 4.26%.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No profile exists for Savannah Condopark, so stack/facing is unresearched — but the URA prints reveal a structure worth recording. The 3BR mix splits into three near-identical sizes that trade as distinct tiers: 1,206sf ~$1,155psf, 1,238sf ~$1,187psf and 1,227sf ~$1,206-1,256psf, with a separate large 3BR type at 1,700-1,800sf. The subject is the 1,238 tier at 31 Simei Rise — the middle tier, consistently 2-5% below the 1,227sf type despite being 11sf larger, which points to a block/facing/aspect difference rather than a size effect. Floor is not disclosed on the listing; within this project the 01-05 vs 06-10 bands show little consistent spread (plot ratio 1.6, low-rise blocks), so floor is a minor value driver here. Worth a /research-development pass to identify why the 1,227 stack out-trades the 1,238 stack before committing.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: Resale-to-resale, same-layout basis: the 1,238sf type printed $1,467,000 (Feb-26), $1,468,888 (Mar-26) and $1,473,000 (Jun-26) — +0.4% over four months — while the project median psf rose 4.4% YoY ($1,155 in 2025 to $1,206 in 2026). Trailing 5yr same-size CAGR is a genuine 8.4%/yr but sits entirely in the 2021-26 bull regime with momentum now -0.581, and the repo's backtest assigns trailing CAGR ~no forward power. 4.0% = D18/OCR forward baseline plus a liquidity/MOP-demand edge, less decay on a 73-year lease. No dated catalyst justifies more.
